title: structRFM — RNA secondary-structure prediction
description: Predict the secondary structure (base pairing) of an RNA sequence with the structure-guided RNA foundation model structRFM. Output is a dot-bracket string over the input sequence; predicted pairs are a model estimate, not an experimentally determined structure.
citation: Zhu et al., An open structure-guided RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction. Nature (2026). https://github.com/heqin-zhu/structRFM

fields.name: sequence
fields.label: RNA sequence
fields.help: A single RNA sequence over A/C/G/U (N allowed for unknown positions).

fields.name: seed
fields.label: Seed
fields.help: Prediction is deterministic; seed is accepted for reproducibility bookkeeping.

example_summary: A tiny 12-nucleotide RNA hairpin (GGGGAAAACCCC), bundled so you can try the pipeline without supplying a sequence.
example_details: A hand-picked minimal hairpin: four G-C pairs closing a four-base loop, whose textbook fold is ((((....)))). It exercises the sequence -> dot-bracket path end to end. Swap in any single RNA sequence over A/C/G/U to predict its structure. Until the real structRFM checkpoint is wired in (M1), the returned structure is a deterministic placeholder, not a structRFM prediction.
notes: source_commit, checkpoint_digest, worker_image_digest and the sequence max_length are provisional until confirmed by the M1 baseline and M4 smoke runs (see IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md).
